title: feat(tools): multi-seat indexable face mills and end mills
body:
## What changed

This PR is the `camcraft-tools` slice of #3646. It adds `milling_cutter.rs`, `milling_cutter_assembly.rs`, `milling_cutter_error.rs` and `milling_cutter_tests.rs`. There is no new crate edge, no ECS, no file I/O, and no change to `ComponentKind`.

- `MillingBody` holds the facts of a cutter body: `DC`, the cutting edge angle `KAPR`, `APMX`, `center_cutting` and an optional seat count. The seats are the body's `CSW1_1..CSW1_N` ports, or one seat port and a seat count. All seats take one shared insert.
- `derive(body, spec, insert)` gives a `MillingCutter`. `MillingCutter::tool(base)` gives the milling `Tool` record. The record has the diameter, the corner radius, `flutes = Some(seat count)`, the flute length and `center_cutting`. The running data (speed, feed, materials, cutting rows) comes from the base tool that the caller gives.
- `MillingCutter::assembled(base, nodes)` puts the cutter into a #3643 spindle assembly. It resolves the nodes itself. Three rules apply (the #4192 review):
  - **One source.** The cutter keeps the body and the insert that it was derived from. The assembly must mount exactly these two components. Another insert or another body is refused by name (`Mismatch`), also on the same diameter.
  - **Every seat.** Each seat port of the body is placed as the mounted insert is. Its cutting point must be on `DC` and in the tip plane, and its axes must be those of the mounted seat in its own radial frame. Thus each seat is the mounted seat turned about the spindle axis (`SeatOff`, with `what` = radius, height, orientation or frame). On a body with one seat port and a seat count, the other seats are copies of that port, so the check of the one port covers them.
  - **The real profile.** A body band inside the cutting depth must be inside the tool profile at the lowest point of the band. The profile includes the corner arc of a bull-nose or a round-insert cutter (`BodyOutside` gives the radius that the tool reaches there). The part above the cutting depth is enclosed over the tool (`HolderProfile::enclose`).
- The law is that the tool is never smaller than the real cutter (Prime Directive):
  - At 90 degrees the diameter is `DC`, and the corner is the nose radius of the insert. The model is exact.
  - Below 90 degrees the edge runs outward. A `DC` cylinder would be smaller than the cutter, so a gouge could pass. Thus the diameter is the reach of the edge at the top of the cutting depth: `DC + 2 * flute_len * cot(KAPR)`. This diameter is not the literal `DC` of the issue. The decision file gives the reason.
  - On a round insert the corner is half the size code (cut down to whole mm). Thus the model corner is never rounder than the insert.
  - `flute_len` is `APMX`, but no deeper than the shortest edge can rise at `KAPR`.
  - The tool's shank holds the part of the inserts above the cutting depth.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3646-multi-seat-cutters.md`.

## Readings

- A 4-seat Ø50 90-degree face mill with `SCMT120408` gives diameter 50, corner 0.8, flutes 4 and flute length 8 (`APMX`). With `APMX` 20 the flute length is 12 (the edge).
- The same mill at 45 degrees with `APMX` 6 gives flute length 6 and diameter 62.
- A 3-seat Ø32 round-insert end mill with `RCMT1204M0` gives corner 6 and flute length 4.
- In a BT40 assembly the gauge length is 95. The tool holds the holder (holder Ø50) and the cutter body.
- Ø50, 90 degrees, `SCMT120408`: a body down to the tip at r 24.8 is refused; the tool reaches r 24.2 at the tip. A body at r 24.2 passes.
- Ø32 round insert `RCMT1204M0`: a body down to the tip at r 15 is refused; the tool reaches r 10 at the tip. A body at r 9.5 passes.

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-tools` lib, `milling_cutter_tests`)

- `a_face_mill_and_an_end_mill_share_one_insert`: a face mill and a shoulder end mill share one insert. An edit of the insert changes the corner on the two mills.
- `a_45_degree_face_mill_cuts_its_edge_reach`
- `a_round_insert_end_mill_takes_half_its_insert_as_corner`
- `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`: the envelope pin. It samples the real meridian outline: the edges, the nose arc, the full insert at 90, 75, 45 and 20 degrees, and a round insert of its metric size and its inch size.
- `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body`: the gauge length and the enclosed body. A body outside the cutter inside the cutting depth is refused, and so are seats off `DC`.
- `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused` (review finding 1): a bull-nose and a round-insert cutter, each with a body that is refused and a body that passes.
- `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` (review finding 2): the selected seat `CSW1_1` is valid. A second seat on Ø80, a third seat 1 mm off the tip plane and a fourth seat turned 10 degrees are each refused by port. A one-port body with a seat count of 4 passes.
- `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` (review finding 3): the shared insert changes to `SCMT120400` before the assembly, and another cutter body. Both are refused.
- The three new pins are the reviewer probes in the new API. The probes in the old API (`assembled(base, resolved)`) failed on `25eca3ba4` on winbuild: 4 of 4 red (bull-nose body, round body, second seat on Ø80, changed insert).
- `seats_that_do_not_take_the_insert_are_refused_by_the_fit_checks`: the #3642 `FitError` (size, shape, kind).
- `degenerate_cutters_are_refused_by_name`: NaN and infinite values, `DC` <= 0, `APMX` 0, a bad `KAPR`, 0 seats, a seat count that does not agree with the ports, 33 seats, a body that is not a tool item, and corners that do not fit.

## The mutation

m1 to m4 ran on winbuild against head `25eca3ba4`. m5 to m10 ran on winbuild against the fix files (`milling_cutter_assembly.rs`). Each one made a pin red, and the clone was restored after each one.

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| m1: below 90 degrees the diameter is `DC` (the literal of the issue) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`, `a_45_degree_face_mill_cuts_its_edge_reach`, `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body` |
| m2: the shank does not hold the inserts (`shank_d = diameter`) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter` |
| m3: the round corner is the size code plus 1 mm (rounder than the insert) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`, `a_round_insert_end_mill_takes_half_its_insert_as_corner` |
| m4: a body outside the cutter inside the cutting depth passes | `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body` |
| m5: the body check uses `diameter / 2`, not the profile (finding 1) | `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused` |
| m6: no radius check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m7: no height check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m8: no orientation check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m9: no check of the mounted insert against the derived one (finding 3) | `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` |
| m10: no check of the mounted body against the derived one (finding 3) | `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` |

## The Windows gate (winbuild)

- Head `1366f4942ea925b12b839aabf109388f1de330df` (the first line of `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-4192-1366f4942.log`), trial-merged with `origin/main` `72890060b` (clean).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the plan has 1 step, `tools suites: lib`. Result: ok, 186 passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane did not run, because no code outside the tools lib changed. This PR is P6, so it gets no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- No app code changed. `crates/app` and the UI do not read the new module yet.
- No operation ran with a derived tool (the plunge refusal and the collision checks on an operation). These need the document record of #3644.

## What is left on #3646

- The app part (`crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`): the document record, the edit of a shared insert that marks the milling operations `Stale`, and the plunge refusal and collision tests on an indexable face mill. This part waits for #3644, which is in work now.
- `tool_material` and cutting rows that come from the insert. The #3642 insert component does not carry them yet.

Changelog: none (domain code only; the user sees it when #3644 stores the cutter)
